I farm for a living, so I keep the plan practical and within what my family can handle. Because some people in my household work off-farm, I will not spread myself too thin with labor-heavy management. My land is 10.1 mu, and my main system is still wheat-maize, so I will keep most of the land in that rotation because it is stable, I know it well, and I can support it with my well irrigation. I will leave a smaller part for cotton because it still brings cash, but it needs more spraying and more careful field work, so I will not put too much land into it. For wheat, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer at a medium level, irrigate a few key times, and aim for steady yield rather than chasing the highest yield. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, follow wheat on the same land, keep inputs solid, and rely on one or two irrigations depending on rain. For cotton, I will use improved seed, give it more potassium and more pesticide sprays than grain crops, and keep the area smaller because it takes more attention. I will mainly use rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale and fits my usual way of working.
